description: "Use when adding or editing translations, locale files, i18n config, or using useT/Trans in packages/i18n. Covers locale structure, adding keys, type safety, and platform entry points."
applyTo: "packages/i18n/**"

# i18n Package Conventions

`@repo/i18n` is the single source of truth for all translations. It uses i18next with a single `common` namespace. Serbian (`sr`) is the **default** locale; English (`en`) is the fallback.

## Entry points — use the right one per platform

| Import path            | Platform                        | Provides                                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@repo/i18n`           | Web (Next.js client)            | `useT`, `Trans`, `useChangeLanguage`, locales/defaultLocale             |
| `@repo/i18n/client`    | Web — explicit client re-export | Same as above                                                           |
| `@repo/i18n/server`    | Web — Next.js server components | `getT`, `initServerI18next`, `generateI18nStaticParams`, `createProxy`  |
| `@repo/i18n/native`    | React Native (Expo)             | `useT`, `Trans`, i18n instance (auto-initialised with LanguageDetector) |
| `@repo/i18n/constants` | Any                             | `LOCALES`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE`, `FALLBACK_LOCALE`, `DEFAULT_NS`            |

Never import from internal paths like `@repo/i18n/src/...`.

## Locale file structure

Translations live in `src/locales/<lang>/`. Each locale exports one `TranslationResources`-typed default object built from feature files:

```
src/locales/
├── en/
│   ├── index.ts      # assembles all feature files into TranslationResources
│   ├── auth.ts
│   ├── common.ts
│   ├── home.ts
│   ├── metadata.ts
│   └── user.ts
└── sr/               # mirrors en/ exactly
```

## Adding a new feature namespace / keys

1. Create `src/locales/en/<feature>.ts` and `src/locales/sr/<feature>.ts` with matching key shapes.
2. Import and spread both into the respective `index.ts`:

```ts
// src/locales/en/index.ts
import { feature } from "./feature";
const en: TranslationResources = {
  ...common,
  metadata,
  auth,
  home,
  user,
  feature,
};
export default en;
```

3. Add the feature to `TranslationResources` in `src/types.ts` if it is a **top-level** key (nested under `metadata`, `auth`, etc. is fine without a types change).

## Type safety — English locale is the source of truth

`src/types.ts` uses the English locale as the TypeScript reference type. Any key present in `en/` but missing in `sr/` (or vice-versa) will cause a type error. Both locales must stay in sync.

```ts
// src/types.ts — do not change the derivation pattern
export type TranslationResources = typeof en;
export type Locale = (typeof LOCALES)[number];
```

## Using translations in components

```tsx
// Web or native client component
import { useT } from "@repo/i18n";

function LoginForm() {
  const { t } = useT();
  return <h1>{t("auth.login.title")}</h1>;
}
```

```tsx
// Next.js server component
import { getT } from "@repo/i18n/server";

async function Page() {
  const { t } = await getT();
  return <h1>{t("auth.login.title")}</h1>;
}
```

## Interpolation

Use double-brace `{{variable}}` syntax in locale strings:

```ts
welcomeBack: 'Dobrodošli nazad, {{firstName}} {{lastName}}!',
```

```tsx
t("auth.login.welcomeBack", {
  firstName: user.firstName,
  lastName: user.lastName,
});
```

## Constants

Always import locale constants from `@repo/i18n/constants`, not from internal paths:

```ts
import { DEFAULT_LOCALE, LOCALES, FALLBACK_LOCALE } from "@repo/i18n/constants";
```
